_comment: LEMONARDO oh-my-posh prompt. The alternative to prompt/midori.omp.json.
install.sh renders this to ~/.config/lemonardo.omp.json; shell/zshrc.midori
points oh-my-posh at ~/.config/midori.omp.json, so switching means editing
that one `--config` path.
THIS FILE NAMES ANSI SLOTS WHERE MIDORI'S NAMES HEXES, and that is not a
style preference -- the hex mechanism does not port, measured rather than
assumed. oh-my-posh has no light/dark blocks: one colour per job serves BOTH
appearances. Midori's palette happens to hold mid-tone accents that straddle
its two grounds, so six hexes work there, with a worst case of 2.76:1 (ochre
on paper). Lemonardo's does not, and deliberately: themes/lemonardo.json
takes light accents from the -800 tier and dark ones from -300/-400, because
a hue legible as small text on bond is not legible on inkwell. Straddling
both with one hex was tried for all six jobs and the best candidate in each
role scored, as min(bond, inkwell):
path + arrow   ansi10 light #105028   1.50:1   <- unusable
git dirty      ansi3  dark  #d58d15   2.37:1
diverged       terracotta   #b03e22   2.42:1
git clean      ansi6  light #1c716e   2.48:1
ahead          ansi2  light #1c763f   2.53:1
separator      faint  light #767d85   3.43:1
A slot NAME is resolved by the terminal per appearance, so each mode gets
its own tier and the straddle problem disappears. Measured on each mode's
own ground, every value below:
lightGreen (10)  #105028  8.24:1 bond   #55e487  8.74:1 inkwell
Worst case 4.60:1, against Midori's 2.96:1. The slot names are from the
schema's own color_string pattern (oh-my-posh 26.14.3): black, red, green,
yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, darkGray, light*, plus bare 0-255.
AND THIS REVERSES A DECISION MIDORI MADE ON PURPOSE, which is the one thing
here a reader must not take as an oversight. prompt/midori.omp.json named
ANSI colours until 2026-08-20 and was deliberately pinned to hex; t3/README.md
holds the reason. t3 exposes no ansi role and no --ansi-* variable, and
hardcodes two bright-on-dark palettes: against a 4.5:1 floor on Midori's
cream, the VGA table medians 2.33 with 11 of 16 failing and the VS Code one
2.48 with 13 of 15. A prompt painting with slot NAMES is unreadable there,
and no terminalForeground fixes it. Truecolor is the way out because t3's SGR
parser returns literal rgb for 38;2;R;G;B.
WHY LEMONARDO GOES BACK ANYWAY, and what it costs. The hex route was tried
first and it does not reach. Searching every value themes/lemonardo.json and
the two ghostty themes declare, within 40 degrees of each Midori token's
OKLCh hue so the roles keep their meaning, the best straddle collapses to TWO
distinct colours for six jobs -- mint.light #2e7d5b at 2.86:1 worst for path,
clean AND ahead, clay.light #a0701d for dirty, error AND the separator. Six
roles rendered in two colours is not a prompt. Midori can pin hex because its
accents are mid-tone and muted; Lemonardo's cannot because its light accents
come from the -800 tier and its dark ones from -300/-400, which is a decision
themes/lemonardo.json makes for legibility reasons of its own.
So the t3 constraint is REAL and is not met here. It does not bind yet: t3
has no Lemonardo theme -- t3/midori-t3.json is the only one -- so the surface
where slot names break does not exist for this design language. If one is
ever made, THIS FILE IS A KNOWN BLOCKER, and the fix is the one t3/README.md
already names (an upstream ansi role, or a custom-CSS hook) rather than a
retreat to hex, which would cost four of the six role distinctions above.
THE JOB-TO-SLOT MAP IS MIDORI'S, re-expressed. Each hex in midori.omp.json
was traced to the slot or role it came from and the slot kept, so the two
prompts mean the same things: path and the arrow on bright green (10), a
clean tree on cyan (6), dirty or behind on ochre (3), ahead on green (2),
the separator on dim text (8). The one role with no slot is `diverged`,
which Midori paints in its terracotta palette role; it takes red (1) here,
the failure slot, because that is the meaning rather than the pigment.
AND THIS IS WHY shell/zshrc.midori NEEDED NO TWIN: its fzf colours are slot
INDICES under --color=16, so it was already wearing whichever palette is
live. Naming slots rather than values is the portable choice across this
whole terminal surface; tmux/lemonardo.tmux.conf is down to two hexes for
the same reason, and herdr/config.lemonardo.toml to four.
